Minutes from an unusual rush
The care crew gathered to discuss calm handling

Attendees were Dylan Wong, Nikhil Ali, and Sasha.

The shift opened with a reminder to keep passenger guidance clear and steady before departure. The team agreed that calm voices, tidy staging, and quick checks help pets settle better and help travelers feel supported. We reviewed crate spacing, water access, and the need to watch for signs of stress during handoff. I asked everyone to slow the pace at the counter when families seem unsure, since a little extra patience prevents confusion later.

The next point focused on cabin care and route setup. <<FACT F040>> Staff noted that the pet area must stay clean, quiet, and ready for the next handoff, with labels matched to the right traveler and pet. We also talked about confirming any special needs early, then repeating them back in simple language so nothing gets missed.

A separate note covered deck setup for the Windmere route. <<FACT F047>> The crew agreed to use the same calm approach there, with one person checking documents while another keeps the pet moving gently through the process. If a traveler seems nervous, the best response is to explain each step without rushing and to keep the animal in sight.

We closed by reminding everyone to report any crate issue, scent concern, or delay right away so the next shift can step in smoothly. The meeting ended.
